focus.jbig: Iran pause = relief rally · but scan is EMPTY into Fed + mega-cap week · stand aside
focus.jtag: U.S. and Iran paused hostilities over the weekend — oil tumbles, futures rally, VIX eases — but the scanner boarded zero and FOMC + four mega-caps + PCE all land this week
focus.jnote: The environment eased over the weekend — but the calendar is a minefield. The U.S. and Iran paused hostilities, with Tehran saying it would hold fire as long as Washington did, and the relief flowed straight into markets: oil dropped over 5% (WTI ~$85, Brent ~$88) as the Hormuz risk premium came out, equity futures rose (S&P ~+0.8%, Nasdaq ~+1.3% led by tech), gold ticked up toward $4,100 as rate-hike fear eased, and the VIX slipped toward ~17.8. That is the good news. The bad news is the schedule: this is the busiest week of the quarter — the FOMC decision Wed 7/29 (hold expected, but a live ~30% hike bet exists), Microsoft and Meta Wed after the close, Apple and Amazon Thu after the close, and June Core PCE Fri. On top of that, today's full-universe scan boarded zero qualifying setups. This is a wait-for-it tape, not a sell-premium-into-it tape.
focus.notdown: Mega-cap tech (MSFT, META, AAPL, AMZN) and chips are catching the relief bid as oil falls and rate-hike fear eases. But be honest: all four report this week — MSFT/META Wed, AAPL/AMZN Thu — so earnings risk sits inside any normal DTE. The bid is real but it is pre-earnings; a bull put here is a coin-flip on a binary print. Watch-only.
focus.notup: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX) is the day's clear laggard as crude gives back the war premium — the fundamental lean is down. But XOM & CVX report this week too, and selling a bear call the morning after a 5% oil drop invites a snap-back on any Iran headline reversal. The disciplined answer with an empty board is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why YELLOW (not GREEN)? Two hard locks. First, the calendar: FOMC Wed 7/29 plus Core PCE Fri are exactly the scheduled events the master prompt says cannot carry a GREEN verdict — and MSFT/META/AAPL/AMZN stack single-stock gap risk on top. Second, and decisive today: the full-universe scanner boarded ZERO names — nothing passed the Type A / B / C filters and 4-VAL. Composite 49 and P(≥1% gap) 33% are benign, but with an empty board and a Fed-plus-mega-cap gauntlet ahead, there is simply nothing to do. Stand aside on new spreads; keep any existing position clear of every print and the Fed. Cash is a position this week.

risks: FOMC decision · Wed 7/29, 2:00 PM ET — a hold at 3.50–3.75% is expected, but markets price a live ~30% hike bet and ~80% odds of a September move. Chair Warsh's press conference is the swing factor — no dot plot this meeting. This is the week's number-one scheduled event.

MSFT & META Wed AMC · AAPL & AMZN Thu AMC — four of the most valuable companies report within 48 hours. After Alphabet's capex-driven sell-off, the bar on AI spending is high; any one gap can move the whole index. Keep every spread clear of these prints.
June Core PCE · Fri — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge lands the same week as the decision. A hot print on top of the recent oil spike would revive the rate-hike narrative and pressure stocks.

Iran pause reversal — the de-escalation driving today's oil drop and relief rally is fragile. Any breakdown re-spikes crude through Hormuz and gaps the whole tape back down — the fastest way this week turns risk-off.
Oil & the 10-year — WTI fell ~5% to ~$85 and the 10Y eased off its ~4.71% spike toward ~4.54%. If oil re-spikes or PCE runs hot, a rate pop back toward 4.7% compounds pressure on equities.

earnings.intro: This is the busiest earnings week of the quarter, stacked on top of the FOMC decision. Microsoft and Meta report Wed 7/29 after the close; Apple and Amazon Thu 7/30 after the close; energy majors XOM & CVX and consumer names (KO, BA, F) are scattered through the week — all alongside the Fed (Wed) and June Core PCE (Fri). A single-stock earnings gap on top of a policy decision is a double catalyst — keep every spread clear of its name's print and out to a DTE that clears the Fed.
